title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
summary: I support first-year students in practical laboratories for CFS2101 Computer Organisation and Architecture, helping them connect theory to working C programs, digital logic and binary arithmetic.
points: Weekly two-hour, in-person lab sessions during the first semester.

Topics: introductory C programming, variables and data types, input and output with scanf and printf, number systems, binary arithmetic, Boolean algebra, logic gates, Karnaugh maps, adders and subtractors.
Most of the work is guided debugging: helping students read their own errors, reason about why a program fails and fix it themselves.
Supporting a mixed-ability group, explaining the same idea in more than one way when the first explanation does not land.

title: Guest teaching, master's-level Applied Cryptography
summary: I taught homomorphic encryption to master's students on the Applied Cryptography module, preparing the lecture slides and practical Python exercises built on the Paillier cryptosystem.
points: Prepared lecture slides introducing homomorphic encryption and the Paillier cryptosystem.
Designed practical Python exercises in which students encrypt values with Paillier, combine ciphertexts and decrypt the result.
Taught alongside the module's academic staff.
